newsitem.title: UK: Eastern Electricity prices stg bond to sell.
newsitem.headline: Eastern Electricity prices stg bond to sell.

text.p: The first sterling Eurobond since the call for the May 1 British election gave a generous pick-up over gilts in order to sell, given the current politicking as well as debate over windfall taxes on utilities, traders said on Thursday.
"Doing something at the moment does mean you've got to price it properly," syndicate manager at HSBC said.
Syndicate manager at joint lead BZW said: "It has been a defensive period in the market since the election call, so we factored the election into the price.
"The high profile government discussions on utilities also meant we could not risk a failure," he said.
Eastern Electricity, the largest of 12 British regional electricity utilities, raised 200 million stg over 15 years.
Eastern Electricity is a unit of Energy Group.
The bond was priced to yield 90 basis points over gilts which sold, at a 99.322 reoffer price, to British institutional investors. The paper pays a coupon of 8.75 percent.

"We felt with at 90 (b.p.) over, we would get a full subscription from people who had previously been a bit defensive in putting money into the market and into the utility sector in general," BZW's syndicate manager said.
"Because the risks in the sterling market in the long end are high, we could not contemplate a failure."
A syndicate manager away from the joint leads said: "It was a very fairly priced transaction so it flew out the door."
HSBC's syndicate manager said the British election was one of the many factors affecting investor sentiment. He said spreads had generally widened and there was some shakiness in the pound.
Syndicate managers have said the campaign period would curb sterling supply, particularly retail-targeted deals which would be hit by investor swings in demand caused by politicking.
Eastern Electricity has one outstanding sterling Eurobond which matures in 2004. It is rated A1 by Moody's Investors Service and A by Standard & Poor's Corp.
